h: How to Shave Seconds Off Your Lap
p: Most first-timers find their biggest gains come from one simple idea: the racing line. Go into a corner wide, cut in to clip the inside of the bend (the apex), then let the kart drift back out wide on the exit. It sounds obvious, but it straightens out the corner and lets you carry far more speed.

Smooth is fast. Jerky steering scrubs off speed, and so does heavy braking in the middle of a bend. Do your braking before you turn, keep your inputs gentle, and get back on the power as early as you dare.
Consistency matters as much as one hero lap. If your times are all over the place, focus on doing the same thing every lap and the quick ones will come.

Don't fixate on the kart in front either. Look up and through the corner to where you want to come out, and your hands will naturally follow. It's the single biggest habit that separates quick drivers from nervous ones, and it costs nothing to try.
Off the track, Brum has loads to fill a day. The canals around Gas Street Basin are lovely for a stroll, and families with a sweet tooth can head out to Cadbury World in Bournville.
